name: Track123
summary: Shopify order-tracking app: a branded tracking page and order lookup on your own store, synced from 1,500+ carriers, with Shopify shipping emails pointed at that page, a dropshipping mode that hides origin details, and PayPal and Stripe tracking sync. Priced on synced orders a month, with a free tier; estimated delivery dates and branding removal sit on the higher Advanced plan.
best_for: Shopify stores shipping from a few dozen to tens of thousands of orders a month, dropshippers included, that want a branded tracking page and order lookup on their own store, PayPal and Stripe tracking sync, and a free tier to start on
skip_if: you need estimated delivery dates, an unbranded page or Klaviyo triggers but ship far fewer than 2,000 orders a month, because all three start on the $49 Advanced tier; your volume swings well past your plan in peak months and you will not set a usage cap; or your fulfilment app rewrites tracking links and you cannot switch that permission off
honest_knock:
The overage is the most expensive order on the ladder. In-plan, Growth works out at 3 cents an order ($9 for 300), and the rate falls as you climb, to about 1.8 cents at 10,000 orders and 1.2 cents at 50,000. On monthly billing every order past your allowance costs 5 cents, and the plan does not stop you at the limit. A merchant wrote in September 2025 that the $9 plan had cost them $46 in a single month without warning; Track123 replied that the store had kept syncing orders past its 300 and advised setting the capped amount for usage charges to $0.01, or whatever figure you are willing to pay. Do that on the first day, not after the first invoice. In our own test on 17 November 2026 Shopify's approval screen for Growth set that limit to $30 per 30 days unless you change it, so a store that runs past its 300 orders can pay up to $39 a month on the $9 plan.

Annual billing swaps the surprise bill for a silent stop. The pricing article says annual plans have no overage, though the listing and the app's billing page print the 5 cent rate on both cycles without that distinction: once the allowance is used up, new orders stop syncing until you upgrade, and the free plan stops the same way until the next cycle. The FAQ adds that after an upgrade only the last 7 days of orders sync again automatically; older ones need a manual sync, and a customer who looks up an unsynced order is told it cannot be found. On a tracking page whose job is to stop 'where is my order' emails, a stalled sync produces exactly those emails.

The features most stores would pay for sit on the $49 tier. Estimated delivery dates, automatic translation of carrier scans, removal of the Track123 branding and the Klaviyo, Omnisend, Slack and Gorgias integrations are all Advanced; Growth at $9 adds custom email notifications, PayPal and Stripe tracking sync, data export and analytics. The critical reviews are about data quality: in April 2026 a US merchant said a UPS parcel due that day showed an arrival more than a week out, and another said the auto-translation had changed a state abbreviation, which Track123 replied it had fixed. The FAQ also warns that a fulfilment app with permission to edit tracking links can overwrite Track123's link with its own. The help centre counts 1,500+ carriers and the vendor's homepage 1,700+. We installed it on a Shopify development store on 17 November 2026, built the tracking page from a sample shipment and read the billing page and Shopify's approval screen for Growth, without approving it.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Growth · per month for 300 synced orders, $0.05 per extra order, with Shopify's default spending limit for those charges at $30 per 30 days in our test
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/track123 and in our own test the same day; read 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-21 there and in the vendor's pricing article on intercom.help/track123, dated 14 July 2026) Three published plans plus Enterprise, priced on synced orders a month; customer lookups are unlimited on every plan. Starter is free for 50 orders a month, and orders past that do not sync until the next billing cycle. Growth starts at $9 a month or $84 a year for 300 orders, with 700 orders at $19 ($180 a year) and 1,000 at $29 ($276 a year). Advanced starts at $49 a month or $468 a year for 2,000 orders and climbs through 3,000 ($69), 5,000 ($99), 7,000 ($129), 10,000 ($179), 15,000 ($249) and 20,000 ($299), then 25,000 ($349), 30,000 ($399), 35,000 ($449), 40,000 ($499) and 45,000 ($549), up to $599 a month, or $5,748 a year, for 50,000 orders. Above 50,000 orders Enterprise is quoted on request. The pricing article says every order past the allowance costs $0.05 on monthly billing, while on annual billing there is no overage and new orders stop syncing until you upgrade. The listing and the app's billing page (17 November 2026) print “$0.05 per extra order” on Growth and Advanced without separating monthly from annual billing, so confirm which applies before you pay yearly. The Shopify listing shows only the first rung of Growth and of Advanced; the full ladder is in the pricing article. Growth and Advanced carry a 7 day free trial, once per store. In our own test on 17 November 2026 Shopify's approval screen for Growth showed $9 every 30 days and, beside it, an app spending limit of up to $30 per 30 days for charges based on use, room for 600 extra orders, and asked for a payment method; the app's billing page listed Enterprise as custom for 100,000+ orders a month. All charges are in USD through Shopify's billing, every 30 days.

compare_with.name: Trackr
compare_with.why: Trackr is the closest comparison in our own dossiers. Its ladder (read 12 September 2026) has no free plan: $10 a month for 400 shipments, $45 for 2,000, $150 for 9,000 and $250 for 18,000, with $0.05 per extra shipment, and every feature on every tier, estimated delivery dates, Apple and Google Wallet and the Klaviyo and Omnisend integrations included. Track123 starts free at 50 orders and keeps estimated delivery dates, branding removal and the marketing integrations for its $49 tier. The prices cross more than once: at 2,000 a month Trackr is $45 and Track123 $49; at 10,000 Track123's $179 is cheaper, because Trackr's $150 tier stops at 9,000; at 18,000 Trackr's $250 beats Track123's $299 for 20,000. A small store that wants delivery estimates pays less on Trackr's $10 plan; a small store that only needs a branded page and lookup pays nothing on Track123.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Track123 on a Shopify development store: the install from the app address in the admin, because the Install button in the App Store did not work for our test tool, the free Starter plan without a card or account, a tracking page that the app said was generated successfully about 1 minute after the install after 5 onboarding screens, the Customize editor with a sample shipment (progress bar, FedEx scans and a map) after about 10 steps, the Billing page with four plans, the Shopify approval screen for Growth (a 7-day trial and a spending limit of $30,00 per 30 days; it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence; nothing approved) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. The live page and any real parcel were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the Install button on the App Store listing (English) did not work for our test tool: the form sent us back to the list of apps without an install. The app address in the Shopify admin (the apps page of the app) showed You don't have this app installed with an Install button, and that worked. The test started at 21:02:53 (the listing loaded). The screen Install app said the app needs access to View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data; Install was clicked and the app was open at about 21:03:40. No plan choice came first: the app starts on the free plan Starter. Onboarding of 5 screens with one click each: Welcome to Track123!, Dropshiping mode Off (not switched on), Importing shipments (Synchronizing your order of last 14 days), Select tracking page style (Slightly rounded, the default) and Your branded tracking page is ready!, with a link to the tracking page on the store. No terms tick box, no account, no card and no phone number was asked. Core action, a tracking page: the page was ready at about 21:04, about 1 minute after the install, and the Dashboard said Your tracking page is generated successfully. and showed Starter with 50 / 50. The live page was NOT looked at, because the development store has a password. The Customize editor (Tracking page, Track order status, Default, Customize) showed a sample shipment (sample number TK123, Order #TK1231039, status Delivered) with a progress bar (Ordered Aug 7, Order Ready Aug 8, In Transit Aug 9, Out for Delivery Aug 16, Delivered Aug 16), Shipping Details with FedEx scans, a map with Current Location and Package Contents Purple Dress x2 with a button Reorder; the sections were Order lookup, Progress bar, Tracking details and a hidden Shipment review widget, and Product recommendation and Instagram feed said Upgrade. The sample with the progress bar stood there at about 21:05, a little more than 2 minutes after the start and about 10 steps in all. Nothing was saved and no theme change was made; the editor said Store header will appear on the live store. The sample said Powered by Track123 on the search form, and the Dashboard said that the branding can only be removed after a store check by the vendor. No real tracking number or real order was used, so the test covers the page and the sample only, not the link with real carriers, the order lookup with a real order or the Shopify shipping e-mails. Plans in the app (Billing, Monthly; an Annual switch says 20% OFF and was not opened): Starter Free with Orders per month 50 and Unavailable after quota is exceeded (Quota reset date: Dec 17, 2026; Available/Total 50 / 50); Growth $9 a month with Orders per month 300 (a list), $0.05 per extra order and Start 7-day free trial; Advanced (RECOMMENDED) $49 a month with Orders per month 2,000 (a list), $0.05 per extra order, Start 7-day free trial and the features Remove Track123 branding, Estimated delivery time, Checkpoint translation and Klaviyo integration; Enterprise Custom with Orders per month 100,000+, $0.05 per extra order and Contact Us. Starter has Branded tracking page, Access to 1500+ carriers, Auto shipment import and Shopify native email notification. The Change plan dialog for Growth (Monthly, $9 a month) listed PayPal & Stripe integration, Google Analytics, Shipment data export, Custom email notification, ROI analytics, Custom shipping status, Product recommendation widget, Gift tracking and an AI CSS Generator (up to 20 a day). Checkout: Start 7-day free trial on Growth opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription: This app bills you for a recurring subscription and usage charges, the Growth Plan, $9,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 7-day free trial ending on 24 Nov., Subtotal $9,00 plus any applicable taxes, Total $9,00 Due 24 Nov, an App spending limit (charged based on use, to a maximum of $30,00 USD per 30 days, which can be updated after approval), and a row Add payment method; the Approve button was greyed out. The screen did NOT say that a test charge would not be billed. Because a payment method was asked and no card may be entered, nothing was approved; Cancel was clicked. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was nothing to cancel in the app. Removing the app goes through Settings, Apps, the row of the app and Uninstall (the menu in the app shows Manage app, Get support, Pin to your navigation and Uninstall): the dialog says that you can no longer use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason had to be chosen (Testing multiple apps) before the uninstall. Differences from the review: the app proposes a spending limit of $30,00 USD per 30 days on the Growth plan, while the review advises a cap of $0.01; and the Billing page shows $0.05 per extra order on Growth and Advanced without any difference between monthly and annual, while the review says that annual plans have no overage (the Annual view was not opened, so that is only noted). The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: real tracking numbers, the link with carriers and the order lookup with a real order, the Shopify shipping e-mails on the tracking page, Klaviyo, PayPal and Stripe, the paid plans (a payment method was asked), the estimated delivery time, removing the branding, the Annual prices and the live tracking page (the store has a password). Clean up: the app was uninstalled at about 21:12 through Settings, Apps and no longer showed under installed apps. No product, no theme change and no e-mail was made, no paid plan was chosen and no card was entered. All our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The Install button in the App Store did not install the app for our test tool; the app address in the admin worked. The approval screen proposes a spending limit of $30,00 per 30 days, the Billing page shows $0.05 per extra order without saying what holds for annual plans, the free Starter plan stops being available after the 50 orders, and the editor shows Powered by Track123 on the free plan.
